chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) said:

I asked him about a man who marries a concubine while having a free wife, he said: 'No (it is not preferred/valid in the sense of equal division). If a man has a concubine and then marries a free woman to her, he must give the free woman twice the share he gives to the concubine.'
Muhammad said: And I asked him about a man who marries a concubine (while having a free wife), he said: 'There is no harm in it if he is compelled to do so.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dividing shares between a free wife and a concubine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a hierarchical distribution of time and maintenance based on the social status of the wife, granting the free woman double the share of the concubine to reflect her higher standing. The ruling of 'no harm' for marrying a concubine when compelled highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in accommodating necessity, distinguishing it from the stricter conditions often applied in Sunni schools regarding polygyny with concubines.
